question: Should the Claws RFC make core Claw lifecycle the canonical owner of shared MCP declarations in `openclaw.json`?
rationale: The implementation establishes durable ownership and cleanup policy over shared operator configuration; code review cannot determine that permanent product boundary while the RFC remains open.

options.title: Defer until RFC approval
options.body: Keep the PR draft, repair URL redaction and proof, then merge only after the RFC and stacked prerequisite explicitly approve core ownership.

options.title: Approve core ownership
options.body: Explicitly accept Claws as the canonical lifecycle owner for exact manifest-declared MCP entries and document the upgrade and operator-override contract.

options.title: Reject core ownership
options.body: Move package-specific MCP lifecycle responsibility to a plugin or bundle-owned surface and close this stack slice.

recommendation.title: Defer until RFC approval
recommendation.body: Keep the PR draft, repair URL redaction and proof, then merge only after the RFC and stacked prerequisite explicitly approve core ownership.
